accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum for England Year 6 ratio and proportion statement (solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping using knowledge of fractions and multiples) and CCSS 6.RP.A.3 (tape diagrams for ratio reasoning). Every number recomputed: £20 in 3 : 2 gives £4 a box, £12 and £8; Sam £18 gives £6 a box and Ali £12; red : blue 5 : 2 with 15 more gives 5 a box, 25 + 10 = 35; challenge £35 in 3 : 4 gives £5 a box and £20; 300 g flour at 5 : 2 gives 120 g sugar; 7 : 3 with 20 more gives 50; 27 in 4 : 5 gives 15 girls; 2 litres at 1 : 3 gives 0.5 litres. Parameterised answers 3a, 5a, 8a and 3a are whole numbers over every range, each with 8 or more combinations.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented ratio errors (NCETM ratio guidance; Hart, Children's Understanding of Mathematics 11–16, ratio chapter): the additive strategy (Sam on £18 so Ali on £17), dividing a total by one term instead of the sum (£20 ÷ 3 = £6.67, £35 ÷ 4), reading part : part as a fraction (3/2 instead of 3/5), putting a total on one bar or a difference on the whole bar, and swapping the order. The wrong-path script produced 'That is Sam : Ali = 2 : 3. Order matters' and '500 ml is all the drink, juice and water together'.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed under the 30% shingle limit, including against flag_ratio.js (part/part, part/whole, per cent) and flag_barm.js (additive bar models for word problems). No other lab sets the value of one ratio box with a slider while a bracket pins the total, one share or the difference, or asks which bracket placement fits a ratio story.

lab_teaches.evidence: Six steps: build 3 : 2 as boxes and see 3/5; share £20 by dragging the box value until the bars total £20; the same ratio with only Sam's £18 known; a 5 : 2 difference of 15; three stories where the learner picks the bar model with the right bracket; then the challenge. Each step finishes with the rule in the banner (total ÷ all boxes, known part ÷ its boxes, difference ÷ extra boxes).

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: Sam's fraction in 3 : 2 (3/5 vs 3/2 vs 2/3), Sam's share of £20 (£12 vs £10 for an equal split vs £6.67 for ÷3), and Ali's share when Sam has £18 (£12 vs £17 additive vs £9). The reveal repeats the learner's own choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions (bigger share, recipe scaling, difference to total, fraction of the whole, class of 27, paint mix) with answer order rotated. Twelve distinct wrong-answer messages name the slip, e.g. 'Divide by all the boxes, not one part: 3 + 4 = 7 boxes' and '1 : 3 makes 4 parts, not 3. 2 litres ÷ 4 = 0.5 litres of blue'.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK grade −0.1 overall (0.6, −2.0, 0.1, 0.5 by paragraph; money amounts read as short words), well under 6.5. Adult notes FK 4.6, under 9.5. The learner sees 'boxes' and 'bracket'; the adult notes name tape diagrams, part : part and part : whole.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content passed with explanation overlap under 12% against every lesson, including 526 (ratio, proportion and per cent). Each kid paragraph carries one method the items test (draw boxes, total ÷ boxes, one known share, a difference). Adult notes give the two curriculum statements, the three-move method and the named mistakes.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 × 640 in light and dark: the story cards stack as three full-width rows and the bracket label under Jo's or the water bar first clipped at the card edge, so the mini bars were moved up and the label tightened; the info card overlapped the feedback box in step 1 and was moved up under the bars. The slider knob is a 26 px circle with a 52 px tall hit band, and − One box / + One box buttons do the same job.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser runs axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every Show me ends with a tick, and the screenshot and wrong-path runs logged no console or page errors. The canvas sits on a light card in dark mode, its aria-label reads the state (e.g. 'Sam bar: 3 boxes of £4, £12 in all. Ali bar: 2 boxes, £8. Total £20'), and every tap or drag has a button.
